Oh wait. I see — looking at the earlier check at 21:20: "app direct: 000" on 38489 — closed. And now app is on 46019. Why wasn't 38489 reused? `resolveDevServerPorts` re-reads ports.json every time. When I manually wrote ports.json with {app:38489,...} around 20:55, no problem. Then the cms serve (94643) ran and… hmm, cms ran first at 21:00 — it should have kept the saved cms:45423 (and in fact it did — 45423 is responding). Then the boards serve (99209) — kept 43781. Then this app serve — allocated 46019 instead of 38489?!

Hmm, wait, actually no. Let me re-check: when `just serve --apps=app` runs, does it call resolveDevServerPorts which rewrites all three ports (even the unselected ones)? Yes — `resolveDevServerPorts(stateDir)` iterates over all DEV_SERVERS and writes the whole map. For app: candidate 38489 — `isPortFree(38489)`… if the OOM-killed app's TIME_WAIT or the kernel still… no, binding to a port in TIME_WAIT still succeeds.

Actually, wait — was there something on 38489 at that moment? The OOM-killed app process was reaped by oom_reaper, but maybe the serve supervisor (fa's just serve --apps=app, pid 91527) was still running and… no, when app died, `serve` should have stopped everything and exited.

Whatever the exact cause (maybe a race where the previous app's Vite was still holding 38489 at the moment of allocation), the result is: ports.json now says app:46019, and nginx.conf says app→38489. Mismatch → 502 on the proxy for app.

Fix: the app dev server is now actually running on 46019 and responding (the log shows bundle complete + watch mode + URL). First confirm 46019 responds, then fix the routing: rerun `just up --detach --no-seed` (fast, containers are already healthy) to re-render nginx.conf from the current ports.json, and reload the proxy.
